heading_path: DETECTING AN EXCESS NUMBER OF SIGNIFICANT TESTS

blocks.content: In addition to providing a quick visual check as to whether the $p$ values follow a uniform, Schweder and Spjøtvoll suggest that these plots can also estimate $n_{0}$. One fits the best straight line until the upturn (i.e., inflection point) near one appears, extrapolating this line to obtain the $n$ value for $1 - p = 1$ estimates the number of true null hypotheses, $n_{0}$. As shown in Figure A4.1, this gives a value very close to 80 (for the open circles), the correct number of true nulls used to generate this figure.
